Subject: Renewal proposal: stepped 24–36 month ramp with surge orchestration and auto-align options

Hi Matthew —

Thanks again for the time last week. Based on our conversation about Aurora's expected Q4 surge and the multi-product rollout next year, I've attached a proposed renewal that blends two things you asked for: predictable committed capacity and the ability to trigger short-term surge headroom. High-level summary in the attachment (Aurora_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf):

- Term options: 24-month (base) or 36-month (discounted)
- Stepped ramp: quarterly committed increases with predefined burst credits in quarters where you expect major launches
- Co-terming: ability to link satellite product units to the primary account for a combined invoice and single SLA
- Auto-align (auto-renew) option with 90-day opt-out window to keep procurement runway predictable

I've also included a draft SOW for the onboarding work and a first-pass pricing workbook (internal_pricing_model.xlsx).

If this looks directionally right, I propose we:
1) Lock a 24/36-month headline term by Sep 17 so we can reserve Dedicated capacity for your Q4 pilot.
2) Finalize co-terming mapping by Sep 24 (I can run a short intake with your TPMs).
3) Target DocuSign by Oct 1 so we have capacity committed pre-launch.

Attachments: Aurora_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf, SOW_Aurora_2027-2029.docx

Thanks — talk soon.

--

Aisha —

Appreciate the detailed packet. A few quick things from our side:

1) Co-terming is a must — we have three product lines that must consolidate under one renewal for finance. Can you confirm whether the stepped ramp can be assigned per product and pooled for burst usage?
2) Auto-renew is okay in principle but procurement will insist on the 90-day opt-out being non-waivable and on a defined overage calculation for burst credits.
3) Legal will want to see the SOW line-itemizing onboarding milestones and acceptance criteria.

If you can send a version that shows per-product ramp rows + a sample invoice cadence, we can circulate to procurement and legal. Also copy me on any internal notes you use to size the Dedicated pool — that helps us when we scope our internal approvals.

Matt

Subject: RE: Aurora renewal — suggested structuring and concession math (internal)

Aisha / Markus —

I've reviewed the Aurora packet and Matthew's ask. Suggestions to keep the momentum while maintaining margins:

- Offer both term bands: 24m (no commit uplift) and 36m with a 10% annual discount on committed tokens. Use an escalator at year boundaries (3% step-up) to account for model price inflation.
- Stepped ramp: represent as per-product committed rows (prod-A, prod-B, prod-C) that roll up into a pooled burst credit bucket. This satisfies finance visibility while leaving them the operational simplicity of a single SLA.
- Burst orchestration: define burst credits as pre-purchased token blocks usable across products; bill overages monthly at a fixed overage rate (we should propose an overage cap for their first year).
- Auto-align clause: keep 90-day opt-out + require 30 days' notice for ramp-down requests impacting Dedicated reservation planning.

Concessions framework (proposal):
- 36m + upfront partial prepay (6 months equivalent) -> additional 4% discount on top of 10%
- If they want hard co-term guarantee across all product units, restrict the burst pool to a defined max utilization (we can add a safety floor to protect capacity).

Operational asks: we need DemandForecast.xlsx inputs from Aurora by Sep 20 so our capacity planning team can reserve the G4 pool. Can you send Matthew a short mutual action plan and a firm list of required procurement/legal items? I'll review pricing spreadsheets and produce a contract-ready redline.

Karthik
Senior Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference
